subject: Post-call: Tail latency acceptance queries & next steps for Veridian
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rao <alex@veridian.ai>, Priya Rao <priya@veridian.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0500
Subject: Post-call: Tail latency acceptance queries & next steps for Veridian

Thanks again for the call this afternoon — good conversation. Summary + a few clarifying questions so we can size the hosted POC and run representative tests: 

Recap (brief):
- Goal: validate end-to-end tail latency (client -> Veridian app -> Redwood hosted inference -> response) for both non-streaming and streaming flows.
- Primary acceptance band you mentioned on the call: tighter p95 target and a guarded p99 target for spikes.

Clarifying questions (please confirm):
1) Target bands: you indicated desired acceptance targets of p95 <= 150ms and p99 <= 400ms for typical user queries (non-streaming). Is that correct for the initial acceptance criteria?
2) Streaming flows: are we measuring end-to-end time-to-first-token and time-to-last-token separately? On the call you mentioned a time-to-first-token SLO of ~120ms and a time-to-last-token window toleration up to 350ms for longer responses — confirm please.
3) Concurrency profile: what peak concurrency should we drive in the POC? Please provide peak concurrent requests and expected sustained qps. For sizing we need both instantaneous concurrency and 5‑minute sustained averages.
4) Request payloads: please share representative request sizes (avg tokens in prompt, avg tokens in response). If you can attach 10 sample request payloads (anonymized), we'll use them in the test harness.
5) Incumbent baseline: what p95/p99 numbers are you currently seeing from your existing provider in the same geography?

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Veridian to confirm Q1–Q4 above and drop sample payloads into the Drive folder (link below).
- Redwood will prepare a hosted test plan and a temporary API key; propose a 3-day POC window (we suggested Dec 28–30) for volumetric and tail-latency runs.
- Redwood infra/solutions will tune batching/kv-cache and streaming concurrency knobs for the test.

Attachments: veridian_latency_testplan.xlsx (blank template) ; redwood_perf_run_20261219.log (example run from a similar customer).

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XyZ-veridian-poc
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/VD-2026-214

Thanks — if helpful I can also put together a short checklist for the Veridian engineers to confirm network egress, proxy timeouts, and TLS config before we start.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0149

From: Alex Rao <alex@veridian.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@veridian.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 17:05:12 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: Tail latency acceptance queries & next steps for Veridian

Sean — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming answers inline: 

1) Acceptance bands: yes, our product team would like to aim for p95 <= 150ms and p99 <= 400ms for the non-streaming, single-turn calls. We recognize p99 will be higher during bursts.
2) Streaming: measurement expectations are: time-to-first-token <= 120ms for interactive sessions; time-to-last-token we expect it to be within 350ms for typical replies (<60 tokens). For long-form streaming (>200 tokens) we'll accept larger tail spikes but would like visibility on partial token timings.
3) Concurrency: for the initial POC please target peak concurrency of 250 concurrent active requests (these are user-facing sessions), and sustained average of 60 qps over the 5-minute window.
4) Request payloads: attaching 10 anonymized prompts to the Drive folder now. Average request size: 35 tokens in prompt, 48 tokens in response; 95th percentile response length roughly 160 tokens.
5) Incumbent baseline: our current provider reports p95 ~220ms and p99 ~480ms in our us-west region under similar traffic (their numbers are what triggered this eval).

Procurement note: procurement will require SOC 2 Type II evidence and basic data processing terms before we can sign any commitment. I'll loop procurement separately.

DocuSign: We'll share a PO/approval once we have the POC acceptance criteria written up.

— Alex
Alex Rao
Head of Product, Veridian AI
alex@veridian.ai

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rao <alex@veridian.ai>, Priya Rao <priya@veridian.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 18:30:45 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: Tail latency acceptance queries & next steps for Veridian

Thanks Alex — that's exactly what we needed. A few scheduling/config notes for the POC: 

- Proposed POC window: Dec 28 08:00 UTC — Dec 30 20:00 UTC. We'll run staged tests: baseline, ramp, sustained soak, and targeted tail-probing.
- Test config we plan to exercise (can adjust based on your infra):
  * Peak concurrency: 250 active sessions (matches your ask).
  * Sustained qps: 60 qps.
  * Token throughput target (sustained): ~38k tokens/sec across the cluster (we'll size GPUs accordingly).
  * Streaming: time-to-first-token instrumentation enabled; measure per-chunk latency and aggregate time-to-last-token.
  * Batching: we'll run two modes — batching disabled (low latency path) and batching enabled (cost-optimized) so you can see tradeoffs.
  * KV/prefix caching: we'll enable prefix caching for repeated prompts where applicable.

- Practical asks for you before the run: open a temporary test endpoint that accepts our traffic (we can also route through your staging if preferred), and confirm any egress/proxy timeouts > 30s so streaming tests won't get truncated.

I'll start building the Redwood test harness and will upload a detailed schedule and test-run checklist to the Drive folder by EOD tomorrow. Ben, Marissa — can you confirm infra sizing and whether we should pre-warm any dedicated capacity?

If these times work for Veridian we'll send a calendar invite and the temporary API key via a secure link.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
